title: Implement and use the designated-variable construction

title: Aggregate Lemma 3.3 per U (one restricted sum per U)
expected: head oracle: ppsz threshold about 273,000 (1.6x lower than T4), e at 2224173 about 0.1996; referee v3 verifies counts
spec:
Head extension (cost model v3, parameter aggregated; read the docstring of assembly_public.py). Lemma 3.3 sums over pairs U <= E with |E| <= q. Summed per U it becomes
  sum_x p_x(x) = sum over U with |U| <= q of sum over x >= U of w_K(|x minus U|) * p_x(1_U),
where K = q - |U| and w_K(m) = sum_{j=0..K} (-1)^j C(m, j). So each U needs ONE restricted sum instead of one per E. The weight depends on x only through the number of ones of x outside U, which is a sum over groups, so the group-by-group computation still works when every group sum is a polynomial in a new variable y.
1. counting.py, class Counter: add three methods.
 - taylor_aggregated(self, t, Zagg=None): S = self.series_vectors(t); loop over U in range(self.N) and skip U with self.pop[U] > self.q; for every other U add Zagg(t, S, U) (a length-J numpy int64 vector mod self.p; use self.Zagg_brute when Zagg is None); count these calls in self.restricted_sums (set it to 0 at the start of every call); return the length-J vector mod p.
 - Zagg_brute(self, t, S, U): g = self.g_U(S, U) has shape (J, N); return the sum over x with (x & U) == U of w_K(popcount(x) - popcount(U)) * g[:, x], mod p.
 - Zagg_group_separated(self, t, S, U): the same value computed like Z_group_separated (same groups, measurement fibres, representatives and eval_clauses), but returning one length-J vector instead of the table over all E. For every combination of fibres keep prod of shape (J, K+1) (powers of z up to z^(J-1), powers of y up to y^K), starting with prod[0, 0] = 1. For every group g build Pg of shape (J, K+1): the sum over the fibre members x_g with (x_g & U_g) == U_g of vals[:, i] times the row [C(c, 0), C(c, 1), ..., C(c, K)] mod p, where U_g = U restricted to the group's bits and c = number of ones of x_g outside U_g. Multiply prod by Pg as polynomials in z (drop z^J and higher) and in y (drop y^(K+1) and higher). After all groups add sum_j (-1)^j prod[:, j] to the total. Return the total mod p. If K < 0 return zeros. Put the polynomial product in a module-level helper mul_zy(A, B, p) and keep all numbers below p before multiplying (int64).
2. Test in scratch_aggregated.py: for Aux(2, 2, 2, 0) and Aux(2, 3, 3, 0), random_formula(6, 9, rng), designated=False and True: (a) for every t compare C.taylor_aggregated(t, Zagg=lambda t_, S, U: C.Zagg_group_separated(t_, S, U)) with C.taylor_direct(t) (equal mod p); (b) repeat on a fresh Counter after setting C.J, C.q = 3, 2; (c) run C.hermite_H0 on the aggregated Taylor data for all t and compare with brute_count(n, clauses); (d) check C.restricted_sums == sum_{s <= min(q, n)} C(n, s).
3. model.py: return aggregated=True as well (pass it as the eighth argument: exponents_over_R(lam, r, Q, Rs, 'tight', delta, True, True)). The optimum moves to a larger r (about 68 at lam = 2.2e6), so widen the r range of your search if needed.
The hidden referee accepts aggregated parameters only if its own hidden checks of taylor_aggregated with Zagg_group_separated pass, so steps 1-2 must be right before step 3 helps.
stop: scratch_aggregated.py shows equality in every case, smoke.py passes, and smoke.py's e at lam=2224173 is at most 0.2010 (the head's estimate is about 0.1996)

title: Clause units (greedy matching) on top of the designated construction
expected: head oracle: ppsz threshold about 194,000 (1.4x lower than T5), e at 2224173 about 0.1784; referee v4 verifies counts and the matching
spec:
Head extension (cost model v4, parameter units; read the docstring of assembly_public.py). If all variables of a clause share one group schedule (a unit), the clause follows that schedule and ALL its occurrences are read directly. Units come from a greedy maximal matching of clauses: at least |F|/7 clauses get matched, so at most 12n/7 occurrences still need replacement rows (2n without units).
1. construction.py: build_design(aux, n, clauses, rng, designated=False, units=False). units=True needs designated=True (raise ValueError otherwise). Draw av and df exactly as now. Then, only if units: go through the clauses in order; a clause with at least 2 variables is matched when none of its variables is in a unit yet; its variables then form a unit: unit_of[v] = the clause's first variable and av[v] = av[first variable] (one shared schedule) for every v of the clause. Variables outside matched clauses are their own unit (unit_of[v] = v). Then designate, for every factor f: count its occurrences per unit (unit_of of their variables); take the unit with the most occurrences (the first such unit in occ order on ties); mark ALL occurrences of f whose variable is in that unit as designated (constant row Prow[0, i, v] = aux.Lden, Prow[k, i] = 0 for k >= 1, no label, no copy, no position, exactly as in T4) and set df[f] = av[v] of one of them. With units=False the result must stay exactly as in T4 (one designated occurrence, the first, per factor). Also return units=True/False and unit_of (numpy int array of length n). M_eff stays the number of non-designated occurrences.
2. counting.py: in Counter.__init__, when des.get('designated') is true, d must be the number of clause occurrences that are NOT designated: count the indices i of des['occ'] whose factor f < len(clauses) and des['desig'][i] is False. (For T4 designs this equals sum(len(cl) - 1).)

Test in scratch_units.py with Aux(2, 2, 2, 0) and Aux(2, 3, 3, 0) on random_bounded_formula(7, rng) and random_formula(6, 8, rng), designated=True and units=True: check that every unit with more than one variable is exactly the variable set of one clause and that its variables have identical av rows; that no clause with at least 2 variables has all its variables outside multi-variable units (the matching is maximal); that check_design gives kernel_condition and P0_delta True; and that the full count (taylor_inclusion_exclusion with Z_group_separated for every t, then hermite_H0) equals brute_count. Print C.J with and without units (with units it must not be larger).
4. model.py: return units=True together with designated=True, aggregated=True, regime 'tight' and delta: pass it to max_log2D(lam, 'tight', delta, True, True) and as the ninth argument exponents_over_R(lam, r, Q, Rs, 'tight', delta, True, True, True). The optimum moves to r about 77 at lam = 2.2e6.
The hidden referee accepts units parameters only if its own hidden checks of build_design(..., designated=True, units=True) pass.

title: Per-point measurement matrices: at point t the swap of position t is free (Chat_t)

Head extension (cost model v6, parameter perpoint; read the docstring of assembly_public.py and NOTES.md). Definition 3.1 of the paper allows a different measurement matrix at every evaluation point t, but Aux uses one matrix Cmeas for all t. At point t the swap of position t keeps every label inside its group at t, so that part of I - M0 costs nothing there. Writing I - M0 by the type of the local factor at position t leaves only the basis vectors psi whose factor at position t is antisymmetric (e_ab - e_ba), with weight m(j - 1) + m(j), where m(j) = 1 - (-1)^j f_I(j, R, A0) and j = js[k] (it counts that antisymmetric factor). So at point t the measurement rows are Psi[k] for the k with an antisymmetric factor at position t and m(js[k] - 1) + m(js[k]) != 0: about half as many rows as Cmeas.
1. construction.py:
   (a) Aux(r, Q, R, A0, perpoint=False): store self.perpoint = bool(perpoint). While building Psi, record typ[k, s] for every basis vector k and position s: 0 for an e_aa factor (choice c < r in local_basis order), 1 for e_ab + e_ba (sign +1), 2 for e_ab - e_ba (sign -1); store self.typ (numpy int8, shape (D, Q)). With perpoint=True add self.Cmeas_t = [Psi[(typ[:, s] == 2) & (F != 0)] for s in range(Q)], where F[k] = m(js[k] - 1) + m(js[k]) computed with exact Python integers (dtype=object; js[k] >= 1 whenever typ[k, s] == 2). Keep self.Cmeas exactly as it is now.
   (b) check_separation: at point t use self.Cmeas_t[t - 1] instead of self.Cmeas when self.perpoint.
   (c) build_design: put perpoint=bool(getattr(aux, 'perpoint', False)) into the returned dict, and when it is True also des['Chat_t'] = a list of Q arrays: Chat_t[t] is built from aux.Cmeas_t[t] exactly as Chat is built from aux.Cmeas (h copies, the same np.add.at over pos_v and pos_y). Everything else stays unchanged.

2. counting.py: in Z_group_separated and in group_structure, right after the line av, df, Chat = ..., use Chat = des['Chat_t'][t - 1] when des.get('perpoint').

title: Equal-pair windows: the interpolation window depends on the number of equal pairs
expected: head oracle: counting ppsz about 52,500, yes/no ppsz about 24,700; decision e at 2224173 about 0.0874; referee v6 checks Aux(..., eadapt=True) (separation, row counts) and exact counts
spec:
Head extension (cost model v6, parameter eadapt; read the docstring of assembly_public.py and NOTES.md). A label u has e = #{s : a_u(s) = d_u(s)} equal pairs. Its antisymmetric count can only use the other Q - e positions and is Bin(Q - e, 1/2), so it sits around (Q - e)/2, not around Q p. Choose the window per e: start a_e = (Q - e - R + 1) // 2 when Q - e >= R, and a_e = 0 when Q - e < R (then every count fits); A0 is ignored. M0 = V0 sum_e f_{I_e}(W0) [N_E = e], where [N_E = e] is the 0/1 diagonal of the labels with e equal pairs; it commutes with every swap, so the support bound (Lemma 4.2) and the degree stay as they are.
1. construction.py: Aux(r, Q, R, A0, perpoint=False, eadapt=False): store self.eadapt = bool(eadapt).
   (a) Move the loop that builds F = (R-1)! f_I(W0) into a method self._Fmat(start): the same loop with A0 replaced by start.
   (b) self.ne = (a == d).sum(axis=1) (equal pairs per label); self.win = {e: a_e for e in range(Q + 1)} with eadapt, and {e: A0 for every e} without. With eadapt: M0s = np.zeros((D, D), np.int64); for every e in np.unique(self.ne): cols = self.ne == e; M0s[:, cols] = self._Fmat(self.win[int(e)])[self.full, :][:, cols]. Without eadapt: M0s = self._Fmat(A0)[self.full, :] (exactly as now).
   (c) For every basis vector k: es[k] = number of positions s with typ[k, s] == 0, starts[k] = win[es[k]] (store self.es, self.starts); inI = (js >= starts) & (js <= starts + R - 1); Cmeas = Psi[~inI]. With perpoint: F[k] = m(js[k] - 1, starts[k]) + m(js[k], starts[k]) with m(j, st) = 1 - (-1)^j f_I(j, R, st).
   (d) check_f: f_I(j, R, st) == (-1)^j for every st in set(self.win.values()) and every j in [st, st + R - 1]; check_eigen: fv[k] = (-1)^js[k] * f_I(js[k], R, starts[k]).

title: Contraction: sum the groups one at a time (Counter.Zagg_contracted)
expected: head oracle (with T10 and T11): yes/no ppsz about 21,560 (T11 about 24,700), #3-SAT about 4,800, brute about 1,000; decision e at 2224173 about 0.0842; referee v7 checks the bond condition and exact counts with Zagg_contracted
spec:
Head extension (cost model v7, parameter contract; read the docstring of assembly_public.py and NOTES.md). At a point t every measurement row touches at most two groups, and a clause of group g sees another group h only through the rows of the pair {g, h} restricted to h: its half-bond pi_{h->g}(x_h). So the sum over x = (x_0, ..., x_{r-1}) of prod_g A_g can be computed one group at a time (variable elimination) instead of enumerating every measurement tuple: after groups 0..k-1, carry a table keyed by the half-bonds between processed and unprocessed groups. The cost model multiplies the measurement term by phi(r), about 1/2.
1. counting.py: add the method Counter.Zagg_contracted(t, S, U). It returns the same length-J vector as Zagg_group_separated(t, S, U): same q, K = q - popcount(U) (return zeros if K < 0), Ky = K + 1, corrections corr[i-1] = (self.X[U] @ S[i].T) % p for i = 1..J-1, weights self.wX, binom_tab[c][j] = comb(c, j) % p, Ugrp and popg as in Zagg_group_separated.
   (a) Cm = des['Chat_t'][t - 1] if des.get('perpoint') else des['Chat'] (as an int64 array); groups[g] = variables v with av[v, t - 1] == g; cl_group[ci] = df[ci][t - 1]; touch[g] = rows of Cm with a nonzero entry in the columns groups[g] (bool array); nt = touch.sum(axis=0).
   (b) For every group g: masks = all 2^k bitmasks of its k variables (as in group_structure; [0] when k = 0). For every other group h: rows_gh = the rows with touch[g] true and no group other than g and h (nt - touch[g] - touch[h] == 0, as integers); keys[g][h][i] = tuple(int(x) for x in the values of rows_gh restricted to groups[g] for mask i) (mod p when self.residue_keys; the empty tuple when there are no such rows or no variables). reps[g][h] = {value: the first mask of group g with that value}.

GF(p^2) arithmetic: an element a + b s is a pair (a, b) of ints in [0, p); s^2 = c, where c is the least x >= 2 with pow(x, (p - 1) // 2, p) == p - 1. Product: (a, b)(a2, b2) = ((a a2 + c b b2) % p, (a b2 + a2 b) % p). Inverse of (a, b) != (0, 0): N = (a a - c b b) % p, Ni = pow(N, p - 2, p), inverse = (a Ni % p, (-b) Ni % p).

title: Edge bits instead of restricted sums per U (Counter.taylor_edges)
expected: head oracle (with T10-T13): yes/no ppsz about 10,100, #3-SAT and brute below 1,000, occ3 about 197,000; decision e at 2224173 about 0.0730; referee v9 checks the two-group support of the rows, taylor_edges against a direct evaluation at every point, and exact and weighted counts
spec:
Head extension (cost model v9, parameter edges; read the docstring of assembly_public.py and NOTES.md). The Taylor data H(t + z) mod z^J are now computed inside the group-by-group contraction with one bit per 'edge' instead of one restricted sum per set U.
Edges: at point t, a replaced occurrence oi (an occurrence of clause f that is not designated: des['desig'][oi] is False, or des has no 'desig') whose variable v = des['occ'][oi][1] lies in group a = des['av'][v][t - 1] different from the clause group d = des['df'][f][t - 1] is an edge. With S = self.series_vectors(t), the series rows S[k][oi] (k = 0..J-1) are zero outside the variables of the groups d and a. A-part: SA[0][oi] = S[0][oi]; SA[k][oi] = S[k][oi] restricted to the variables of group d for k >= 1. B-part: SB[0][oi] = 0; SB[k][oi] = S[k][oi] restricted to the variables of group a for k >= 1. For every other occurrence SA = S and there is no B-part.
Because every clause is multilinear in its occurrences, H(t + z) = sum over sets E of edges with |E| < J of sum_x w(x) prod_f D_f prod_{oi in E} B_oi, where D_f = 1 - prod_l u_l(A_l) if f has no edge in E, and D_f = -(prod_{oi in E, oi in f} u'_oi) * prod_{l in f, l not in E} u_l(A_l) otherwise; u(y) = 1 - y for a positive literal and u(y) = y for a negative one, u' = -1 for a positive literal and +1 for a negative one. Every summand factorises over the groups, so the contraction can carry the bits of the open edges.
1. counting.py: add the method Counter.taylor_edges(t). It returns the same length-J vector as taylor_aggregated(t) (mod self.p; weights self.wX; with self.residue_keys the half-bond keys are residues, exactly as in Zagg_contracted).
   (a) Use self.group_structure(t) and self.contract_structure(t) exactly as Zagg_contracted does (groups, cl_group, grp_mask, keys, reps); edges, SA and SB as above; cl_occ = self.cl_occ.
   (b) A state is (key, O, c): key = the half-bond key of Zagg_contracted; O = frozenset of the edges whose bit is 1 and exactly one of whose two groups (d or a) has been processed; c = the number of edges whose bit is 1 among those decided so far. Start with T = {((), frozenset(), 0): unit}, unit = length-J int64 vector [1, 0, ..., 0].
   (c) For g = 0, 1, ..., r - 1 (future = g + 1..r - 1): new_edges = the edges with one group equal to g and the other in future; close_edges = the edges with one group equal to g and the other < g; b_side = the edges whose variable group a is g. For every state (key, O, c) with value val: cons, past, rest and every combo of future representatives exactly as in Zagg_contracted (xs = own masks of cons + past + the combo masks; Xs = their bits; Xg = the bits of the own masks only). For every subset N1 of new_edges with c + len(N1) <= J - 1 (itertools.combinations by size): bit(oi) = (oi in O) for close_edges, (oi in N1) for new_edges.
       - A-series of every occurrence oi of a clause of group g: coefficient 0 = (Xs @ SA[0][oi]) % p, coefficient k >= 1 = (Xg @ SA[k][oi]) % p (a (J, len(cons)) array).
       - D_f for every clause f of group g (cl_group[f] == g) with E_f = its edges with bit 1, as in the formula above (truncated series products mod p, like eval_clauses).
       - B-series of every edge oi in b_side with bit 1: coefficient k = (Xg @ SB[k][oi]) % p.
       - contrib = wX[own mask] times the product of all D_f of group g times the product of those B-series (a (J, len(cons)) array of truncated series).
       - For every own mask in cons: new key as in Zagg_contracted, O2 = (O - set(close_edges)) | set(N1), c2 = c + len(N1); newT[(newkey, O2, c2)] += truncated series product of val and that mask's column of contrib (mod p).
   (d) T = newT after each group (return zeros of length J if it is empty). At the end every O is empty; return the sum of the values of all states mod p.
   Pitfalls seen in an earlier attempt: (i) any cache of clause values must be keyed by (clause, bit pattern), not by the bit pattern alone, otherwise clauses with the same pattern share one value; (ii) the A-series of an occurrence that is not an edge uses its full row S; (iii) the weight wX of the own mask multiplies every contribution exactly once.
